cards.context: You have not placed an order or arranged a delivery this week.
cards.body: A driver tried to deliver your parcel. Reschedule today at metro-parcel-confirm.example and pay the $2.15 route fee.

clues.explanation: An unexpected delivery is used to ask for a small payment.

cards.explanation: The delivery does not match anything you ordered, and the message directs you to an unfamiliar payment site.
cards.safeAction: Check orders in the retailer or carrier app you already use instead of following the text link.

cards.context: You do not own cryptocurrency and did not ask anyone to recover an account for you.
cards.body: Your dormant wallet has earned $1,840. Reply START now to release the funds before the recovery window closes.

clues.explanation: The sender tries to begin a conversation around money you did not expect.

cards.explanation: A surprise balance and a closing deadline are designed to make you respond before checking the claim.
cards.safeAction: Do not reply. If you use a financial service, open its official app yourself to review your account.

cards.context: You have not applied for a grant or requested emergency assistance.
cards.body: You qualify for a $900 household grant. Send a photo of your ID and bank card to complete the same-day deposit.

clues.quote: photo of your ID and bank card
clues.explanation: The message requests highly sensitive documents and payment information together.

cards.explanation: A grant you never sought is being used as a reason to collect identity and card details.
cards.safeAction: Do not send documents or card images. Verify any benefit through an independently found official contact.

cards.context: You did not request a password reset and no support conversation is open.
cards.body: We stopped a password change. Text back the code we sent so our agent can lock the account for you.

clues.explanation: A legitimate verification code should stay private, even from someone claiming to be support.

cards.explanation: The sender is trying to obtain an authentication code that could be used to take over your account.
cards.safeAction: Keep the code private and check account security only through the app or website you open yourself.

cards.context: Yesterday you booked a cleaning with Oak Dental for Tuesday at 10:30 am.
cards.body: Reminder: your cleaning is Tuesday at 10:30 am. Reply C to confirm or call the clinic number already saved in your contacts to reschedule.

clues.explanation: The time matches the appointment you personally booked.

cards.explanation: This is a routine reminder for a known appointment and does not ask for money, credentials, or sensitive information.
cards.safeAction: Confirm if the details match your appointment, or call the clinic using its known number.

cards.context: You put the novel 'The Glass Harbor' on hold through the library catalogue.
cards.body: Your hold, The Glass Harbor, is ready at Riverside Library until 18 October. Bring your library card to collect it.

clues.explanation: The message identifies the exact title you placed on hold.

cards.explanation: The pickup notice matches a hold you made and only gives collection details.
cards.safeAction: Check the hold in your library account if you want an independent confirmation.

cards.context: You cancelled your Harbor Gym class in its app a few minutes ago.
cards.body: Your 6:00 pm Pilates booking has been cancelled. No charge was made. Your booking reference is HG-4418.

clues.explanation: The update matches the cancellation you just completed.

cards.explanation: This is a confirmation of a change you initiated and it does not direct you to a payment or sign-in page.
cards.safeAction: Keep the reference if needed and review the booking in the gym app.

cards.context: You bought two tickets for Maple Theatre's Friday matinee from its box office website.
cards.body: Your Friday matinee starts at 2:00 pm. Doors open at 1:30 pm. Your ticket QR codes remain in your Maple Theatre account.

clues.explanation: The message corresponds to the show you already purchased.

cards.explanation: The text provides practical event information for a known purchase and asks for nothing in return.
cards.safeAction: Open the box office account you already use if you need to view the tickets.

cards.subject: Final notice: design subscription overdue
cards.context: You do not have a design subscription and have not received an invoice from this company.
cards.body: Our records show an unpaid annual renewal of $289. Avoid collection action by paying today at studio-billing-center.example.

clues.explanation: A threat is used to pressure payment for a service you do not use.

cards.explanation: An unexpected invoice combined with a threat and a payment link is a phishing pattern.
cards.safeAction: Do not use the link. Check any real subscriptions through the official service you already know.

cards.subject: Interview shortcut approved
cards.context: You have not applied for a job with this company and did not contact a recruiter.
cards.body: You were selected without an interview. Complete the payroll form today by entering your personal email password to verify identity.

clues.explanation: An employer has no reason to request the password for your private email account.

cards.explanation: The unsolicited job offer uses an impossible payroll requirement to steal account credentials.
cards.safeAction: Do not share a password. Research employers independently before engaging with a job offer.

cards.subject: Confidential task before the meeting
cards.context: Your director normally uses the internal work chat for requests, and there is no meeting scheduled today.
cards.body: I need 12 digital gift cards for guests. Buy them now, email the codes back, and keep this between us until the meeting.

clues.explanation: Gift card codes can be spent immediately and are difficult to recover.

cards.explanation: The sender impersonates a manager, creates secrecy and urgency, and asks for gift card codes.
cards.safeAction: Verify the request with your director through the established internal channel before buying anything.

cards.subject: Files scheduled for deletion in 2 hours
cards.context: Your Cloud Vault app shows that you have ample storage and no deletion notice.
cards.body: Your storage limit was exceeded. Restore access in 2 hours by signing in at cloud-vault-restore.example.

clues.explanation: A very short deadline is meant to prevent careful verification.

cards.explanation: The warning contradicts the account information you can see in the real app and pushes an unfamiliar sign-in link.
cards.safeAction: Open the storage app yourself and check account notices there.

cards.subject: Your Friday matinee ticket receipt
cards.context: You just bought two Friday matinee tickets through Maple Theatre's official box office page.
cards.body: Thank you for your purchase. Order MT-80317 confirms two Friday matinee tickets. Total paid: $36.00. No action is required.

clues.explanation: The receipt includes the order reference shown after your own purchase.

cards.explanation: This is a receipt for a transaction you just completed, and it does not request credentials or an additional payment.
cards.safeAction: Keep the receipt and view the order through the box office account if necessary.

cards.subject: Orientation room confirmed: Library 204
cards.context: You enrolled for Pine Coast University's new-student orientation and selected the afternoon session.
cards.body: Your afternoon orientation session is confirmed for Library 204 on 21 October. Bring photo ID for check-in; no online form is needed.

clues.explanation: The room detail corresponds to the session you registered for.

cards.explanation: The email confirms a known registration and provides attendance details without asking you to click, pay, or sign in.
cards.safeAction: Compare the details with your enrollment calendar if you would like to verify them.

cards.subject: One item changed in order FB-10592
cards.context: You placed grocery order FB-10592 this morning and selected 'allow substitutions' at checkout.
cards.body: For order FB-10592, Green Valley oats are unavailable. We will substitute Harbor Mill oats at the same price unless you update the order in the app by 4:00 pm.

clues.explanation: The order number is the one from your recent grocery checkout.

cards.explanation: The message matches an active order and the substitution preference you selected; it does not request payment information.
cards.safeAction: Use the grocery app you already have open if you want to change the substitution.

cards.subject: Service visit tomorrow, 9:00–11:00 am
cards.context: You scheduled a washing-machine repair with Cedar Appliance Service and received this time window at booking.
cards.body: Your repair visit is booked for tomorrow between 9:00 and 11:00 am. The technician will show work order CS-7784 on arrival. No payment is due at the door.

clues.explanation: The work-order number matches the repair booking you made.

cards.explanation: This is a routine reminder for a service appointment you arranged and it makes no request for a link or sensitive data.
cards.safeAction: Keep the work-order number and call the service company through its known contact if the time changes.

cards.context: You did not request computer support and your computer is working normally.
cards.body: Caller: 'We are from Device Shield. Your laptop is sending virus reports. Install our remote tool now so I can remove the infection before your files are locked.'

clues.explanation: An unsolicited caller wants remote access to your device.

cards.explanation: Real support providers do not normally call out of the blue and pressure you to install remote-control software.
cards.safeAction: Hang up. If you are concerned, contact your device provider through its official support channel.

cards.context: You have no unpaid government fee and did not receive an official letter about one.
cards.body: Caller: 'This is the National Revenue Desk. An enforcement officer will visit today unless you pay $480 using a crypto kiosk while I stay on the line.'

clues.explanation: Government agencies do not demand payment through cryptocurrency machines.

cards.explanation: The caller combines a threat of enforcement with an unusual, hard-to-reverse payment method.
cards.safeAction: Hang up and independently find the official agency contact before discussing any alleged debt.

cards.context: Your sister is at home and has not contacted you about an emergency.
cards.body: Caller: 'Your sister caused an accident and cannot talk. Send $1,200 by instant transfer in the next ten minutes or she will be arrested.'

clues.explanation: The caller uses urgency to stop you from checking on your sister independently.

cards.explanation: A fabricated family emergency and a demand for an immediate transfer are common impersonation tactics.
cards.safeAction: End the call and contact your sister or another family member through a known number.

cards.context: You have not made a transfer or started a bank login, and no bank appointment is scheduled.
cards.body: Caller: 'I am from Northbank fraud prevention. Read the six-digit code that just arrived so I can cancel the transfer for you.'

clues.explanation: The caller is asking for a security code that could authorize their own action.

cards.explanation: A caller cannot safely verify a transaction by asking you to reveal an authentication code.
cards.safeAction: Do not share the code. Hang up and call the number printed on your bank card.

cards.context: The Meadow Pharmacy app notified you earlier that your refill was being prepared.
cards.body: Caller: 'Your prescription refill is ready for collection until Friday. We are not taking payment by phone; please bring your usual ID when you visit.'

clues.explanation: The caller gives collection information and explicitly does not seek payment details.

cards.explanation: The call follows a status update from the pharmacy you use and provides a routine pickup reminder.
cards.safeAction: Collect the refill or call the pharmacy using its verified number if you have a question.

cards.context: You are expecting a washing-machine technician today between 9:00 and 11:00 am under work order CS-7784.
cards.body: Caller: 'This is Cedar Appliance Service. Our technician for work order CS-7784 is delayed by twenty minutes and will arrive around 10:15 am.'

clues.explanation: The caller has the booking reference for your expected repair visit.

cards.explanation: The update concerns a real appointment you scheduled and only changes the expected arrival time.
cards.safeAction: Wait for the technician or call the service company through its established number if needed.

cards.context: Your calendar contains a Pine Coast Clinic check-up tomorrow afternoon.
cards.body: Caller: 'This is a reminder that your check-up is tomorrow at 3:40 pm. Please arrive ten minutes early. We do not need any information from you on this call.'

clues.explanation: The time matches the appointment recorded in your calendar.

cards.explanation: This is a basic reminder for an appointment you know about, with no request for data or payment.
cards.safeAction: Attend as planned or call the clinic through its known number if you need to reschedule.

cards.subject: Critical virus scan completed
cards.context: The alert appeared while you were reading an ordinary news article, and you had not started a security scan.
cards.body: 18 threats found! Call 0800-555-0199 immediately or install ShieldFix from browser-security-help.example to prevent permanent damage.

clues.explanation: A web page is trying to move you to an unsolicited support call.

cards.explanation: A browser page cannot credibly run an emergency device scan, and the alert pushes a phone number and unfamiliar download.
cards.safeAction: Close the tab without calling or installing anything. Run a scan only with security software you already trust.

cards.subject: Device configuration update required
cards.context: You did not open system settings or request an update; the pop-up appeared inside a free wallpaper app.
cards.body: Install the Secure Device Profile from device-config-update.example within five minutes to keep using your phone.

clues.explanation: An unrelated app is pressuring you to install a device-management profile.

cards.explanation: The alert appears in the wrong place and asks you to install a profile through an unfamiliar site.
cards.safeAction: Dismiss the pop-up and check operating-system updates only in your device settings.

cards.subject: You are today's selected winner!
cards.context: You did not enter a contest; this appeared after tapping an advertisement in a game.
cards.body: Claim your tablet in the next 90 seconds. Pay a $3.99 verification charge at prize-shipping-center.example.

clues.explanation: The supposed prize requires an unexpected payment.

cards.explanation: A surprise prize, short countdown, and payment demand are warning signs of a prize scam.
cards.safeAction: Close the advertisement and do not submit payment details.

cards.subject: Update ready for Harbor Notes
cards.context: You opened the official App Store, selected Harbor Notes from your Purchased list, and tapped its Update button.
cards.body: Harbor Notes version 4.2 is ready to install. Tap Update to download the version you selected.

clues.explanation: The prompt follows an update action you initiated in the official store.

cards.explanation: This is the expected confirmation after you asked the official app store to update a known app.
cards.safeAction: Install it if it is the app and update you intended to select.

cards.subject: Guest network terms
cards.context: You joined the clearly labelled Harbor Cafe guest Wi-Fi network after asking staff for its name.
cards.body: Welcome to Harbor Cafe guest Wi-Fi. Read the terms and tap Accept to connect. No password, payment, or account sign-in is requested.

clues.quote: No password, payment, or account sign-in is requested
clues.explanation: The captive portal only asks you to accept network terms.

cards.explanation: The page follows joining a network that staff confirmed and does not ask for credentials or money.
cards.safeAction: Accept the terms if the network name still matches the one staff provided.

cards.subject: Save changes before closing?
cards.context: You have been editing an unsaved poster in the Canvas Draft app and just tapped Close.
cards.body: You have unsaved changes to Autumn Festival Poster. Choose Save Draft, Discard Changes, or Cancel.

clues.explanation: The dialog names the document you were actively editing.

cards.explanation: The save dialog is an expected local warning after you try to close an edited document.
cards.safeAction: Choose the option that matches whether you want to keep the changes.

cards.subject: Reminder: team brunch in 15 minutes
cards.context: You created a 'team brunch' calendar event for today and set a 15-minute notification.
cards.body: Team brunch starts at 12:30 pm at Juniper Room. Snooze or view the event details.

clues.explanation: The reminder names the event you added to your own calendar.

cards.explanation: This is a locally scheduled reminder for a known event and offers only normal reminder controls.
cards.safeAction: Snooze it or open the calendar event if you need directions.
